characters.name_or_role: the man (seesaw, black cloak, glasses) - sole speaker
personality_traits: self-deprecating and quick to preempt criticism ("I've already lost an argument that hasn't started yet")
defensive/anxious under a partner's silent scrutiny
deadpan sarcastic humor delivered in a flat, resigned tone rather than agitated
conflict-avoidant but wordy - fills silence with rationalizing rather than confronting directly
expressions: 0:00 neutral, half-lidded tired eyes as he opens his mouth to speak ("Don't")
~0:02 eyebrows lift slightly, mouth pulled into a small incredulous purse on "like what"
~0:04-0:05 brow furrows, mouth opens wider as he leans into the complaint ("I've already lost...")
~0:05 ("At") most animated beat - eyes widen behind glasses, head tilts back as he touches his face
~0:07-0:08 ("first"/"you") expression softens into a tired, pleading half-smile as he finishes the line
gestures: hands gripping the seesaw handle, torso upright and still through the opening lines
~0:05 both hands rise together to his glasses/face in a flustered, self-conscious adjusting motion (coincides with the most emphatic word of the line)
hands return to the handle by the end of the line, body settling back into stillness
large black cloak draped over his shoulders shifts like wings when his hands lift, visually exaggerating the defensive gesture
characters.interactions_notes: He is the only one who speaks and the only one who moves expressively; he never fully holds her gaze, instead glancing off or reacting to her stare rather than meeting it head-on, reinforcing that he is on the back foot in this exchange.

characters.name_or_role: the woman (seesaw, brown sweater, bun) - silent counterpart
personality_traits: stoic and quietly judgmental - conveys disapproval entirely through a held stare rather than words
patient but skeptical, unmoved by his preemptive excuses
composed and still, functioning as the emotional 'straight man' against his fidgety wordiness
emotional_range: faint, simmering disapproval that never escalates or breaks
expressions: 0:00-0:08 (entire clip) near-static half-lidded, narrow-eyed stare directed at him - the 'look' referenced in the on-screen title ('That Look') - shows essentially no change across the whole sequence
mouth remains flat and closed throughout, no smile or frown shift even as his tone escalates
gestures: hands resting motionless on the seesaw handle for the full duration
upright, unmoving posture contrasted against his shifting cloak and hand movements - her stillness itself reads as the gesture/punchline
characters.interactions_notes: She never speaks and barely moves, but her fixed stare is the scene's entire source of tension - he is visibly reacting and defending himself against a judgment she hasn't voiced. The physical seesaw, balanced and static between them, mirrors the power dynamic: she holds steady ground while he does all the emotional and verbal work to try to shift it.
